notes: NULL READ, cause external (AWS WAF challenge). *** THE METHODOLOGICALLY IMPORTANT RECORD OF MY SIX, AND IT CUTS THE OTHER WAY: here the register looks RIGHT and the Bancroft Library catalogue looks WRONG. *** Hoffman's 1862 table and Bancroft's Hist. Cal. (twice, at III, 656 and in the Pioneer Register at IV, 714) both make Victor Linares the 1837 grantee and William D. Foxen the claimant, exactly as the register has it. Only the digicoll MARC record says Foxen was the grantee, and it does so in a form that is itself the tell. *** A REUSABLE RULE FOR THE REST OF THE PASS. *** In this record the MARC 700s assign ONE person (Foxen) all three roles - Claimant, Grantee and Patentee - and there is no separate grantee heading at all. Compare my other five: where the grantee genuinely differs from the claimant, the same catalogue does list them separately (Temecula: Ortega/Stokes/Valdez as Grantee vs Vignes as Claimant; Tequepis: Joaquin Villa as Grantee vs Antonio M. Villa as Claimant; Tepusquet: Olivera as Grantee vs Cota as Claimant; El Toro: Estrada as Grantee vs Walters as Claimant). SO: when a case file's MARC 700 block collapses Claimant + Grantee + Patentee onto a single name, the grantee attribution is an artifact of the cataloguing, not evidence, and must not be used to contradict the register. Two of my six show this collapse - rancho-tinaquaic and rancho-todos-santos-san-antonio - and both are cases where Bancroft's grant list names a DIFFERENT grantee. Any agent using digicoll metadata as a substitute for the decree during this outage needs this rule or it will manufacture false errors. PROSOPOGRAPHY: 'Guillermo Domingo Foxon' = William Benjamin Foxen, 1800-1874, English sailor who came on the Courier in 1820, baptised Wm Domingo, married Eduarda Osuna (or Olivera), naturalised 1837 (Bancroft, Hist. Cal. III, 762) - the Foxen of Foxen Canyon. Victor Linares was a San Diego soldier of 1826, majordomo at San Luis Obispo 1839-40 and militia alferez, grantee of Canada de los Osos in 1842, juez at San Luis in 1846 (Bancroft IV, 714). Two entirely distinct men; this is not a spelling variant. RE-READ TARGETING (free, no PDF needed): MARC 300 '1 portfolio (54p.)' - the smallest file of my six, 60.9MB; MARC 500 'Spanish text on pages 8-13, 21-24'. The 1837 concession and the 1842 boundary instrument should both sit in stamped pp. 8-24, so --pages 1-30 settles it. THE ONE LIVE QUESTION IS THE GRANTING AUTHORITY, and it is more interesting than a copy error. Figueroa died 29 Sept 1835; the grant is dated 17 Oct 1835, inside the interim. Bowman attributes it to Castro. But Bancroft records that the case turned in part on 'the right of the ayuntamiento to grant this rancho, which was claimed by the military company', which raises the possibility that the instrument issued from the Monterey ayuntamiento rather than from the acting jefe politico. The register's 'the interim government' is vague enough to be either right or evasive. A re-reader should photograph the signature block and the attestation, not just the dispositive clause. *** RE-READ TARGETING - DO NOT USE --pages 1-30 HERE EITHER. *** MARC 300 '1 portfolio (124p.)'; MARC 500 'Spanish text on pages 20-34, 48-58, 67-76, 85-86'.
